create.name: Beginner's Mind Zen Center
create.bio:
Beginner's Mind Zen Center is a neighbourhood zendo in a quiet residential street in Northridge, in Los Angeles's San Fernando Valley, close to California State University, Northridge. It was founded in 2003, first as Northridge Zen Center, by Peter and Jane Schneider, two early students of Shunryu Suzuki who had served as his attendants at Tassajara in its first years and later spent more than two decades studying in Japan. Peter, a former director of Tassajara and president of San Francisco Zen Center, received transmission from Mel Weitsman; Jane, who received transmission from Grace Schireson, is the founding abbess. Since Peter's death in 2025, vice abbot Heiji Toshin Spencer Levy has helped guide the sangha with head of practice Myokan Chris Burnham.

The centre's name comes from Suzuki's phrase, and its programme is meant for beginners and long-time sitters alike. Zazen with open discussion runs on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, an early sitting on Wednesdays is held online, and Saturday mornings add a Dharma talk and service; everything can be joined on Zoom. Roughly monthly one-day retreats and two-day sesshin include private interviews with the teachers, and no membership is needed to take part. Many of its talks are posted on its YouTube channel.

courses.title: Daily Meditations
courses.description: Regular sittings open to all: Tuesday and Thursday evenings with zazen and discussion, a Wednesday dawn sitting on Zoom, and Saturday mornings with zazen, walking meditation, a Dharma talk and service, in person and online.

courses.title: Zazenkai (Full Day)
courses.description: A one-day Saturday retreat held about once a month, from 8 am to around 5 pm, with periods of sitting and walking, a Dharma talk, service and the chance of a private interview with a teacher.
courses.price: Suggested donation: $15 for members and $25 for non-members

courses.title: Sesshin (Multi Day)
courses.description: Two-day weekend retreats of sustained zazen, walking meditation, service, meals and talks; participants may come for both days, one full day or part of a day.
courses.price: Two full days: Members $30, Non-members $40; one full day: Members $15, Non-members $25; partial day: Members $10, Non-members $15

free_resources.title: How to do Zazen
free_resources.description: A beginner's guide to sitting at home: choosing a place, sitting on a chair or cushion, holding the hands, counting the breath from one to ten, and letting thoughts come and go without chasing them.

free_resources.title: Dharma Talks
free_resources.description: Recorded talks from the zendo, including an introduction to the centre, with a link to its YouTube channel of more than two hundred videos.
